SpaceXAI and Cursor are in the process of becoming a single company, but first, the two firms are releasing an all-new iPhone and Mac app called Grok Bot.

According to SpaceXAI’s announcement, Grok Bot is a new kind of AI agent described as “AI teammates you can give real work to.”

Each Bot gets its own computer, then signs into the apps and services you already use to take on work across inboxes and other tools.

SpaceXAI says Bots can complete jobs end to end, only returning when approval is needed.

You can message one “like a colleague,” the company says, and the agent will remember conversations, learn preferences, and improve with more use.

Grok Bot launches in beta today on Mac and iOS. Windows and Linux desktop versions are also available. Android is listed as coming soon.

Access is initially restricted to SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, and Cursor Teams Premium subscribers.

You can learn more from the official announcement here.

There’s been an unusually large drop in the price of AAPL stock so far this week, losing roughly $25 per share in the two days since the WWDC keynote.

While some are inevitably speculating that investors weren’t impressed by Apple’s AI announcements, there are other factors at play …

Yahoo Finance was one of those to attribute the slide to the WWDC announcements.

Apple Inc shares were down 4% on Tuesday afternoon after the company’s annual developer conference left some investors questioning the pace of its artificial intelligence rollout, even as analysts broadly viewed the event as a step forward […] Despite the reported improvements, analysts flagged meaningful limitations.

Siri AI will launch in beta later this year for supported devices set to English and will not be available initially in the European Union on iOS or iPadOS. The feature is also excluded from China due to regulatory hurdles. That leaves two markets which, together, account for roughly 35% of trailing 12-month iPhone shipments, according to Morgan Stanley.

US stock futures declined on Wednesday after the US launched “self-defense strikes” against Iran in response to the downing of an American helicopter, escalating tensions in the region. Investors also awaited the release of US inflation data for fresh signals on the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook, after stronger-than-expected jobs figures last week reinforced expectations of an interest rate hike before the end of the year.

articles.title: Letting You Be A Complete Psychopath Reveals The Scale Of Fable‘s Ambition
articles.subtitle: Fable Gamescom 2026 Playground Games RPG Fable lets you kill every NPC. If you want to violently depopulate the world in Fable, you absolutely can. People will start appearing again eventually, but in the meantime it’ll be a ghost town.
articles.author: Kotaku
articles.content:
Fable Gamescom 2026 Playground Games RPG

Fable lets you kill every NPC. If you want to violently depopulate the world in Fable, you absolutely can. People will start appearing again eventually, but in the meantime it’ll be a ghost town. Most games would make the characters immune or flash a game-over screen if the player went off-script. Fable is trying to revel in it.

“Yeah, you could absolutely get down to nobody living,” says Playground Games cofounder Ralph Fulton at Gamescom 2026, the game director on Xbox’s upcoming open-world fantasy RPG epic.

Some locations, however, are harder than others to purge entirely. Fulton uses the game’s biggest town, Bowerstone, as an example.

“In theory, yes, and in practice, I think it would be extremely difficult to do that. Let me take you out of Bowerstone and put you in a smaller village? More feasible.”

The challenge lies in what happens when the murders start. Firstly, NPCs run and hide. Secondly, guards show up. Albion’s finest will start hunting you, and they won’t stop. “They are the game’s defense mechanism against you being a psychopath,” says Fulton.

If you can deal with endlessly respawning guards, however, there’s technically nothing preventing you from taking out everyone. Of course, this being a Fable game, there will be consequences for your actions.

For starters, if you kill a shop owner, you’ll no longer be able to use them to buy stuff. It makes sense. After all, the owner’s dead. This is a world in which local businesses, like tailors, pubs, and bakeries, are staffed by NPCs with their own routines, and if you disrupt that, as Fulton says, “it’s kind of on you.”

You’ll also earn a thoroughly negative reputation, but there’s a caveat. This reputation is only for the settlement in which you committed the foul acts. In Albion, news does not travel far. Visit a different town or village, and residents there may have an entirely different perception of you, based on their personal experience. This means you can be a saint in one place and a sinner in another, experimenting with your morality without becoming universally known as a complete bastard.

That morality system is one of Fable ‘s signature features, but the new game makes changes to it that have proved controversial with some fans. Previously, a given act on your part was either considered good by everyone, or evil by everyone. Here, however, while some may despise you for certain actions, others may admire you for them. Additionally, here your ethics are expressed as a word cloud floating to the left of your head, and temporarily visible as you enter a new location.

It’s built from thousands of adjectives like “charismatic,” “friendly,” “hard-working,” and if you ever decided to kill everyone in sight, “violent..” So, why the change?

“We came at it from the perspective of looking at the world around us. Not necessarily a video game world, but the real world around us. How morality exists. And it felt to us like there just wasn’t any objective good, or objective evil. You and I can observe the same thing, and probably come to completely different moral judgments on it.”

This subjectivity is something Playground Games were adamant in including. Morality here is in the eye of the beholder. Fable, though, doesn’t stop there. This greater moral complexity even accommodates contradiction, mixing and matching sometimes opposing adjectives to form your own unique personality blend.

“I could be a charismatic thief, right? You can combine some things which are morally grey, and just see how people respond.”

Some players, however, might choose more underhanded ways to strike at the populace. For instance, making people homeless. Fulton describes playtesters buying people’s properties and raising the rent, thereby forcing them to live on the streets.

Just like with mass murder, you can also evict entire towns en masse, a possibility Playground Games had to prepare for. The developers provide a fixed slot on the street for each individual NPC in case their housing situation ever gets compromised.

“It kind of staggers me a little bit, but yeah, people seem really obsessed with that. To the point that every one of our settlements has to be designed to support the entire population sleeping rough.” If you’re sadistic enough, you can make hundreds of Albion townsfolk live in squalor while you strut around like a king.

But what’s the end goal? What can you actually buy with the profits of your sprawling property empire?

articles.title: ChatGPT update adds Apple Messages integration on Mac
articles.subtitle: Well, this seems interesting. ChatGPT’s latest update adds a new Mac integration: the ability to work with conversations from Apple’s Messages app. The feature works with iMessage, SMS, and RCS.
articles.author: 9to5Mac Apps
articles.content:
Well, this seems interesting. ChatGPT’s latest update adds a new Mac integration: the ability to work with conversations from Apple’s Messages app. The feature works with iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now includes an Apple Messages plugin

The new Apple Messages plugin lets ChatGPT read and search chats on a Mac, and prepare and send messages.

OpenAI says it is available across all plans in the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, with support in both ChatGPT Work and Codex.

That access raises privacy and control questions, so OpenAI stresses that sending remains gated by user approval under the default settings.

Users should take care before granting persistent approval. OpenAI’s plugin guide details the risks and how to revoke access.

It also lists a known issue involving tasks that disable approval prompts: “If your task is set to Full access or otherwise disables approval prompts, Apple Messages may be unable to show the confirmation needed to send. Switch to Ask for approval or Approve for me and try again.”

How OpenAI’s Messages plugin works on the Mac

OpenAI explains that the optional Messages plugin runs locally on the Mac. Like other ChatGPT/Codex features including Computer Use, it relies on macOS system technologies like AppleScript and Accessibility.

The optional Messages plugin is not like the sketchy server-related hacks that try to bring iMessage functionality to Android. It’s simply using files on your Mac with your permission when prompted.

And unlike Siri AI, it doesn’t rely on an index of content from Messages. ChatGPT for Mac only uses the data when directed and with permission.

As you can see below, once enabled by the user, ChatGPT is super clear in what it does with messages, especially sending on your behalf when asked.

For these reasons, it shouldn’t be a privacy concern for Apple. The data exists as files on your Mac, and you need to give ChatGPT permission to work with the files. OpenAI also isn’t the only AI company to develop similar tools. It’s just a benefit of the Mac being a more capable operating system than mobile platforms.
